on 19 May, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13654 of 2022
Applicant :- Sudeep Kumar Maurya

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Raman Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of applicant, is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Dr. Gyan Singh learned A.G.A. for the State.
3.
This second bail application has been filed by the applicant with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in case crime No.564 of 2022 under Section 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC, Khairighat, district Bahraich.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that prosecutrix is aged about 22 years and he has invited attention of this Court towards the WhatsApp chatting between the applicant and the prosecutrix.
The WhatsApp chatting indicates that they are in love.
He has also annexed screen shot in which the prosecutrix and applicant both are seen chatting together and has filed pendrive of audio chatting along with supplementary affidavit dated 12.4.2023.

It has been submitted that she made allegation under Section 164 CrPC against the applicant because of family pressure otherwise,
she is consenting party.
The medical report also does not support the prosecution case.
He has Sudeep Kumar Maurya vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

1 further submitted that the applicant has also transferred money in the account of the prosecutrix which has been annexed as Annexure No.SA-1 to the supplementary affidavit dated 12.4.2023.
He has submitted that the applicant has no criminal history and he is in Jail since 20.9.2022.

5. On the other hand, learned AGA has opposed the bail and has submitted that the statement under Section 164 CrPC indicates that the applicant has committed rape, therefore, bail application is liable to be rejected.
6. Considering the over all facts and circumstances of the case, the WhatsApp chatting between the applicant and the prosecutrix, it is a fit case for bail.

7. Let the applicant Sudeep Kumar Maurya be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

8. It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
